title: JANUS POSS-I — Human Witness Temporal Control
purpose: Add a source-independent human-observation layer to the POSS-I nuclear-association investigation. Test whether people reported star-like lights or other aerial anomalies preferentially near nuclear-test dates, while explicitly measuring the non-nuclear human-report baseline on other dates.

primary.source: US National Archives / Project Blue Book case files and finding aids
primary.record_scope: Project Sign / Grudge / Blue Book case files, 1947-1969, including witness questionnaires, correspondence, analysis and case-control sheets.
primary.why_primary: Most Blue Book reports were collected on a standardized Air Force questionnaire recording date, hour, description and other observational details. The case files are chronologically arranged and NARA provides an index by date and location.
primary.important_boundary: A Blue Book report is evidence that a report was made and investigated; it is not proof that the reported object was extraordinary or extraterrestrial.

retrospective_sensitivity.source: National UFO Reporting Center (NUFORC) public event-date index
retrospective_sensitivity.why_secondary: Historical reports can retain exact claimed occurrence dates and useful morphology language, but many 1950s events were submitted decades later. Reporting delay, memory reconstruction, media exposure and survivorship bias are therefore material.
retrospective_sensitivity.data_handling_rule: Do not scrape, redistribute or mirror row-level NUFORC data. Use public browsing and aggregate derived statistics only, respecting the source terms of service.

STARLIKE_WITNESS.definition: Descriptions dominated by one or more star-like, point-like, sparkling, luminous, white/blue/yellow points or compact lights without a clearly resolved craft body.

FORMATION_LIGHTS.definition: Multiple compact lights/points maintaining or changing formation. Kept separate because formation descriptions can arise from aircraft, balloons, birds, meteors or memory reconstruction.

RESOLVED_CRAFTLIKE.definition: Disk, cigar, cylinder, triangle or other reports explicitly describing a resolved body. Never merged with STARLIKE_WITNESS for the primary morphology test.

RADAR_ONLY.definition: Radar reports without contemporaneous visual witness confirmation. Separate endpoint.

ASTRONOMICAL_OR_METEORIC.definition: Reports ultimately classified as stars, planets, meteors, fireballs, auroral phenomena or similar astronomical explanations. Retain as a negative/control phenotype rather than discard.

preliminary_open_retrospective_monthly_a.source: NUFORC public reports-by-event-month index as publicly visible on 2026-08-15
preliminary_open_retrospective_monthly_a.analysis_window: 1951-01 through 1957-04, aligned with the active nuclear-test portion of the current POSS-I study window
preliminary_open_retrospective_monthly_a.nuclear_calendar: JANUS frozen strict open SIPRI/IAEA-derived calendar used by the public POSS-I reconstruction

season_trend_adjusted_negative_binomial_.warning: This negative model-dependent coefficient is not admitted as evidence that nuclear tests suppress reports. The dataset is retrospective, sparse and subject to major reporting-selection effects.

preliminary_open_retrospective_monthly_a.preliminary_conclusion: No positive monthly human-report enhancement is visible near nuclear-test activity in the retrospective NUFORC layer. A count of nuclear events within a month is essentially uncorrelated with report count in this first pass.

critical_non_nuclear_baseline_examples.description_summary: Witness report describes six rows of six objects perceived as stars moving in formation and making a 90-degree turn.
critical_non_nuclear_baseline_examples.nuclear_context: No strict-calendar nuclear test occurred in July 1952; the preceding strict tests were 1952-06-01 and 1952-06-05, and the next was 1952-10-03.
critical_non_nuclear_baseline_examples.interpretation: Direct example that star-like/formation morphology exists in the human-report record outside nuclear-test windows.

critical_non_nuclear_baseline_examples.source: US National Archives / Project Blue Book
critical_non_nuclear_baseline_examples.description_summary: NARA identifies a series of multiple UFO sightings over Washington, DC on this date as part of the well-documented 1952 reporting wave.
critical_non_nuclear_baseline_examples.nuclear_context: No strict-calendar nuclear test occurred in July 1952.
critical_non_nuclear_baseline_examples.interpretation: Strong historical non-nuclear reporting-wave control: high public/military observation activity can occur without a contemporaneous nuclear test.

additional_starlike_morphology_example.description_summary: Witness described two bright white-and-blue objects as stars, reportedly pursued by jet fighters.
additional_starlike_morphology_example.use: Morphology example only; outside the current POSS-I study endpoint of 1957-04-28 and therefore not used in the primary temporal test.

blue_book_context.historical_1952_wave_rule: The 1952 reporting wave must be represented explicitly as a non-nuclear/media-observation-pressure control; it may not be treated as background noise to be averaged away.

required_exact_date_analysis.primary_unit: human sighting report occurrence date, not submission/publication date
required_exact_date_analysis.primary_comparison: STARLIKE_WITNESS incidence on strict nuclear day -1, day 0 and day +1 versus matched non-nuclear control dates
matched_controls: no nuclear test within the selected exclusion radius
separate high-media-attention dates from ordinary dates
required_exact_date_analysis.never_pool_without_indicator: Source system and report delay must be explicit model terms; Blue Book and NUFORC may not be silently pooled as if they were sampled by one process.

bias_controls.reporting_delay: Retain event date and report/submission date separately. A report filed decades later cannot be treated as contemporaneous surveillance.
bias_controls.media_wave: Control for major publicity waves such as Washington 1952 because publicity changes propensity to report and remember.
bias_controls.population_exposure: Human report counts require population/visibility/reporting-opportunity normalization and cannot be directly compared to photographic plate counts.
bias_controls.night_day_visibility: Stratify by local time/daylight where reliable; STARLIKE reports are strongly visibility-dependent.
bias_controls.astronomical_confounders: Moon, bright planets, meteor showers, aurora/geomagnetic activity and known fireballs should be joined where date/location precision allows.
bias_controls.aviation_military_activity: Known aircraft, training, missile/rocket and balloon activity must remain explicit alternative explanations.
bias_controls.duplicate_event_reports: Multiple witnesses to one event are different from independent events. Maintain witness_count and event_cluster_id separately.
bias_controls.geography: Global nuclear-test dates should not imply local physical exposure. Distance from test site and line-of-sight/environmental plausibility are separate covariates.

admission_gates.pass: Every report has source system and stable record reference or source index provenance.
Occurrence date/time is separated from report/submission date.
STARLIKE_WITNESS morphology rules are frozen before nuclear-window labels are inspected for the detailed case set.
Multiple witnesses of one event are not counted as independent events without explicit clustering.
Matched non-nuclear dates are analyzed with the same inclusion rules.
Contemporary Blue Book and retrospective NUFORC layers are reported separately before any combined model.
Permutation/block controls preserve year/season/source reporting structure.
A temporal association, if found, remains a reporting/observation association until physical linkage survives geography, astronomy and artifact controls.

next_required_work: Build the primary exact-date Blue Book case index from NARA public records for 1949-11-19 through 1957-04-28.
Blind-label STARLIKE_WITNESS / FORMATION_LIGHTS / RESOLVED_CRAFTLIKE / RADAR_ONLY / EXPLAINED_ASTRONOMICAL phenotypes from case summaries before joining nuclear-window flags.
Run exact lag -4 through +4 and matched non-nuclear date controls.
Test the 1952 Washington wave as an explicit high-reporting non-nuclear control epoch.
Only after the Blue Book primary layer is complete, use NUFORC as retrospective sensitivity and never as the source of the confirmatory result.
